functions.funcDef: Generate and control thrust for all phases of flight (SDD §5.1.1 — four podded turbofans 'provide thrust for all phases of flight').
functions.subDef: Produce commanded forward thrust from four engines across the flight envelope. In: thrust/reverse commands from flight deck (§5.1.4). Out: thrust. Independence: engines 1-4 numbered outboard-to-outboard, left/right pairs in separate zones (§5.1.5) — single engine loss does not cause total thrust loss (§5.1.3 'continue following the loss of any one engine').

functions.funcDef: Generate and control thrust for all phases of flight (SDD §5.1.1).
functions.subDef: Provide ground deceleration by reverse thrust from the two inboard engines (§5.1.2 'Thrust reversers are fitted to the two inboard engines only'). In: reverse command, weight-on-wheels + radio-altimeter agreement (§5.1.2). Out: reverse thrust. Independence: separate control action inhibited in flight by WoW/RA, distinct from forward-thrust production.

functions.funcDef: Position primary and secondary aerodynamic surfaces to control the aircraft about all axes across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Position ailerons and multi-function spoilers to command roll (§5.3.2). In: inceptor/autopilot commands via FCS computers, HYD B/C actuation (§5.3.4). Out: surface position. Independence: ailerons on HYD B and C (§5.3.2 'the ailerons from B and C') — roll axis fails independently of pitch/yaw actuation.

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to control the aircraft across the envelope (SDD §5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Position the all-moving trimmable stabiliser and elevators to command pitch (§5.3.2). In: inceptor/autopilot commands, HYD A/C actuation (§5.3.2 'the elevators from A and C'). Out: surface position. Independence: mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim exists (§5.3.2) — pitch retains a degraded path with all three FCCs lost.

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to control the aircraft across the envelope (SDD §5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Position the split upper/lower rudder segments to command yaw and counter asymmetric thrust (§5.3.2). In: inceptor/autopilot/FCS, HYD A (upper) and B (lower) (§5.3.2 'rudder segments are supplied from systems A and B'). Out: rudder position. Independence: two segments each with own actuation and hydraulic supply — sizing case is outboard engine-out at V1 with max blade (§5.3.3), single rudder supply loss must still leave sufficient authority.

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to control the aircraft across the envelope (SDD §5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Extend/retract double-slotted Fowler flaps and full-span slats to set the lift configuration for take-off and landing (§5.3.2). In: crew selection, two independent power drive units. Out: high-lift position to performance computation (§5.3.4). Independence: two PDUs through a common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes at each section (§5.3.2) — common torque shaft is a recorded commonality, not fully independent.

functions.funcName: Decelerate and control the aircraft on the ground
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground, absorb landing/taxi loads on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces, and provide braking and directional control on the ground (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.subName: Support aircraft on ground and provide flotation
functions.subDef: Support the aircraft and spread footprint pressure to the level semi-prepared surfaces require (§5.6.1). In: HYD A retraction/extension with free-fall alternate (§5.6.2). Out: ground support, gear position (§5.6.4). Independence: free-fall extension independent of hydraulic pressure (§5.6.3); gear-leg/bogie count is preliminary (§5.6.2).

functions.funcName: Decelerate and control the aircraft on the ground
functions.funcDef: Provide braking and directional control on the ground (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.subDef: Provide carbon multi-disc wheel braking with anti-skid to decelerate within the 1,800 m landing requirement (§5.6.2, §5.6.3). In: HYD B normal / HYD A alternate / accumulator emergency (§5.6.2). Out: deceleration. Independence: dual hydraulic supply plus accumulator sized to six full applications with all three systems lost (§5.4.3).

functions.funcName: Decelerate and control the aircraft on the ground
functions.funcDef: Provide directional control on the ground (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.subDef: Provide ground directional control by hydraulic nose-wheel steering commanded from tillers and rudder pedals (§5.6.2). In: HYD, crew commands from tiller/pedals (§5.6.4). Out: nose-wheel angle. Independence: mechanical disconnect for towing (§5.6.2) — distinct control path from braking.

functions.funcName: Provide access to and secure the payload
functions.funcDef: Provide straight-in hold access via the nose visor and maintain the pressure boundary when closed (SDD §5.7.1) — the door's behaviour, not its structural load path.
functions.subName: Open and close the nose cargo door
functions.subDef: Move the upward-hinging visor to open/closed for straight-in loading (§5.7.2). In: HYD A with electric backup drive, ground command (§5.7.4). Out: door position to ground handling panel (§5.7.4). Independence: hydraulic with electric backup; cannot operate in flight (§5.7.6). Note: door structural load path is explicitly treated as structure (§5.7.3) and is NOT a function.

functions.funcName: Provide access to and secure the payload
functions.funcDef: Secure the door closed as part of the pressure boundary (SDD §5.7.1).
functions.subName: Lock and confirm nose door closure
functions.subDef: Engage twelve rotary latches and eight locking pins and confirm lock status, with a pressure interlock preventing unlock while the hold is pressurised (§5.7.2). In: separate lock-actuator hydraulic supply, dual dissimilar sensing, ECS residual differential <0.1 psi (§5.7.4). Out: lock status to flight deck and take-off configuration monitor (§5.7.4). Independence: dual dissimilar and independently routed lock-sensing circuits (§5.7.2).

functions.funcDef: Receive, position and restrain a single blade of up to 72.6 t along the full hold length and maintain restraint through all flight and ground load cases (SDD §5.8.1).
functions.subDef: Maintain longitudinal restraint by two tension straps per saddle across nine saddles, tensioned by electric winches and mechanically locked (§5.8.2). In: electrical power to winches, loading plan (§5.8.4). Out: strap tension and saddle engagement to flight deck (§5.8.4). Independence: loss of any one strap carried by neighbours (§5.8.3); hold floor hard points have no redundancy (structure, §5.8.3).

functions.funcDef: Monitor payload restraint integrity (SDD §5.8.2).
functions.subDef: Instrument every strap continuously and annunciate loss of tension, with two adjacent stations annunciated as a restraint condition (§5.8.2). In: electrical power to the tension loop (§5.8.4). Out: restraint status to flight deck and take-off configuration monitor (§5.8.4). Independence: single instrumented loop — coverage is a recorded item (§5.8.3), i.e. NOT redundant.

functions.funcName: Control cabin pressure and condition the air
functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air to the flight deck and hold and control the fuselage pressure differential (SDD §5.9.1).
functions.subDef: Control cabin/hold differential to the low hold differential schedule (~8,800 m equivalent, preliminary) via two controllers and two outflow valves with a pneumatic backup and independent mechanical relief (§5.9.2). In: bleed/electrical power, WoW, door position (§5.9.4). Out: differential pressure and cabin altitude to avionics and crew-oxygen logic (§5.9.4). Independence: either outflow valve sufficient; relief valves protect independently of the control system (§5.9.2). Note: hold differential is preliminary (§1.2).

functions.funcName: Control cabin pressure and condition the air
functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air to the flight deck and hold (SDD §5.9.1).
functions.subDef: Supply conditioned air to the flight deck and hold as separate conditioning zones via two air-cycle packs fed through a cross-bleed manifold (§5.9.2). In: engine/APU bleed, ram air, electrical power (§5.9.4). Out: conditioned air (§5.9.4). Independence: either pack from either side through the cross-bleed manifold; single-pack operation permitted with reduced hold schedule (§5.9.3).

functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice accretion on surfaces, inlets and probes where accretion is unacceptable, for flight in the icing envelope (SDD §5.10.1).
functions.subName: Protect airframe and inlets from ice
functions.subDef: Protect wing leading edges and engine inlet cowls with hot bleed air and heat the stabiliser leading edges in six independently controlled electrical zones (§5.10.2). In: cross-bleed manifold bleed, electrical power (§5.10.4). Out: ice protection status and zone health, bleed demand to ECS (§5.10.4). Independence: bleed protection available from either side; electrical zones independently supplied, lost zone annunciated (§5.10.3).

functions.funcDef: Prevent ice on probes and detect icing conditions (SDD §5.10.1).
functions.subDef: Electrically heat probes, static ports, windshields and two ice detectors, and provide advisory ice detection with automatic or manual activation (§5.10.2). In: electrical power, TAT/airspeed, crew selection (§5.10.4). Out: ice detection advisory to flight deck (§5.10.4). Independence: two ice detectors of the SAME type — commonality recorded as an item for examination (§5.10.3).

functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host the alerting (SDD §5.11.1).
functions.subDef: Drive four display units and two HUDs from three display processors on dual redundant networks, with an independent standby instrument for attitude/airspeed/altitude (§5.11.2). In: air data/inertial from three reference units, electrical power, navigation signals (§5.11.4). Out: displays to crew, commands to autopilot/autothrottle (§5.11.4). Independence: standby instrument shares no supply, sensor or processing with the primary displays (§5.11.3).

functions.funcDef: Host the alerting that tells the crew what has failed and what to do (SDD §5.11.1).
functions.subDef: Consolidate every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with associated procedures (§5.11.2). In: data from every aircraft system, electrical power (§5.11.4). Out: alerts to the crew (§5.11.4). Independence: two independent alerting processing channels (§5.11.2).

functions.funcDef: Detect fire and overheat in the zones where they must be detected and provide the means to extinguish or suppress (SDD §5.12.1).
functions.subDef: Provide dual-loop continuous fire detection per engine nacelle and APU compartment (AND logic, degrading to single-loop), plus overheat detection on bleed ducts and gear bays and smoke detection at nine hold stations (§5.12.2). In: DC essential bus power, WoW, APU state (§5.12.4). Out: fire/overheat warnings to crew alerting (§5.12.4). Independence: two loops routed on opposite sides of each zone, separately clipped (§5.12.5).

functions.funcDef: Provide the means to extinguish or suppress fire (SDD §5.12.1).
functions.subDef: Discharge two extinguisher bottles per engine pair (cross-plumbed to either nacelle) and a dedicated APU bottle (automatic when unattended) (§5.12.2). In: hot battery bus power to discharge circuits, crew fire-handle commands (§5.12.4). Out: discharge status, automatic APU shutdown/fuel isolation (§5.12.4). Independence: discharge supplied from hot battery bus so available with all generation lost (§5.12.5). Note: hold carries detection but NO suppression — a recorded decision to substantiate (§5.12.2).

functions.funcDef: Supply breathing oxygen to the flight crew for depressurisation, smoke/fume events and the descent/diversion that follow (SDD §5.13.1) — captured as a behaviour; the gas store is the means.
functions.subDef: Supply oxygen to four quick-donning full-face mask stations with demand regulators from two cross-connected cylinders (§5.13.2). In: crew donning action, cabin-altitude signal from ECS, DC power for indication only (§5.13.4). Out: oxygen to mask stations, cylinder pressure/status to flight deck (§5.13.4). Independence: either cylinder capable of supplying the crew at reduced reserve; regulators independent per mask (§5.13.3).

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of forward thrust generation
fha.effAc: No propulsive thrust available; aircraft cannot sustain level flight and forced descent follows.
fha.effCrew: Crew face an unpowered glide/forced-landing situation with very limited options.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of thrust with no means to sustain flight leads to loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric forward thrust across the aircraft
fha.effAc: Yawing/rolling moment from thrust asymmetry; directional control demand up to the sizing case for an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to maintain directional control with rudder/asymmetry compensation.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A large thrust asymmetry at the outboard 28 m arm is the directional-control sizing case; uncompensated it is a large reduction in safety margins. Magnitude is not bounded by the function definition — confirm. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous thrust not matching commanded setting
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the condition does not bound the magnitude or direction of the thrust error (over- vs under-thrust) nor whether it is symmetric or asymmetric, so no single aircraft effect can be derived. Need the bounded error case(s) to state an effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced available forward thrust
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the magnitude of thrust reduction is unbounded by the function definition — a slight shortfall and the loss of a whole engine give effects two severity classes apart. Need the bounded reduction case(s) (e.g., one-engine-out at V1) to state an aircraft effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded reverse thrust deployment
fha.effAc: On the ground, uncommanded reverse on an inboard engine produces deceleration/asymmetry during rollout or taxi.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to detect and stow/retard the affected reverser.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify without fixing the flight phase that drives the class. In flight the SDD states deployment is inhibited by WOW + radio-altimeter agreement with a mechanical sleeve lock, so the credible case is on the ground; but whether an in-flight case remains credible after interlock failure, and the ground-case magnitude, are not bounded by the function definition. Confirm the applicable phase envelope.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of roll control authority
fha.effAc: No means of commanding or arresting bank; the aircraft cannot be manoeuvred about the roll axis by any means.
fha.effCrew: Crew unable to maintain wings-level or execute a turn; no reversion path restores roll control.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of a primary trajectory-control axis with no reversion leaves the crew unable to control the flight path across all phases; effects support loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous pitch response to crew command
fha.effAc: Aircraft pitches contrary to or in excess of commanded input, producing an unintended and potentially uncontrollable flight-path excursion.
fha.effCrew: Crew command produces a wrong-sense or excessive pitch response; recovery may be impossible if the error opposes crew input, particularly in low-energy or low-altitude phases.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An erroneous response on a primary trajectory-control axis can drive an uncontrollable flight-path excursion; in low-altitude phases the effects support loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded pitch motion with no crew command
fha.effAc: Aircraft pitches with no crew input, producing an unintended flight-path departure the crew must detect and counter.
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise an uncommanded pitch excursion and override it; success depends on available authority and margin, which is not stated for this condition.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncommanded pitch departure on a primary axis can develop into an uncontrollable flight-path excursion, notably at low altitude; the aircraft-level effects support loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded pitch divergence below detection threshold (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: A slow pitch divergence develops without annunciation; with no crew action the excursion is allowed to grow, degrading the flight path toward an out-of-trim or envelope-limiting condition.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties and take no corrective action because the divergence is below the detection threshold; recovery capability once recognised is not stated.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Crew-unaware case: with no annunciation the crew take no action and the divergence develops unchecked on a primary axis; proposed Catastrophic but the divergence rate and time-to-effect are not in the provided material and could support Hazardous instead — confirm against FCS dynamics. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded pitch authority within manoeuvre limits
fha.effAc: Reduced pitch control authority while the aircraft remains within its manoeuvre limits; reduced margin to envelope boundaries.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew attention to hold pitch within a narrower available range; the aircraft remains controllable within limits.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Definition bounds the condition to within manoeuvre limits, so the aircraft effect is a reduction in safety margins/functional capability rather than loss of control; proposed Major (significant reduction) but whether the reduction is 'significant' vs 'large' depends on remaining authority, which the function definition does not quantify. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of pitch control authority (all pitch-control means lost, including elevators and the stabiliser-trim reversion path)
fha.effAc: Aircraft cannot be trimmed or controlled about the pitch axis; uncontrolled flight-path departure with no remaining means of recovery.
fha.effCrew: No control input available in pitch; crew unable to arrest a pitch divergence.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of pitch control with the mechanical reversion path also lost leaves no means to control flight path; effects support loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded pitch authority outside manoeuvre limits (pitch control retained but insufficient for required manoeuvres)
fha.effAc: Reduced pitch authority below that required to manoeuvre within the envelope; large reduction in safety margins, particularly in the take-off, approach and landing regimes.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to fly within the reduced authority; limited ability to counter gusts or configuration changes.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Pitch authority insufficient for required manoeuvres represents a large reduction in functional capability and safety margins short of total loss. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded pitch authority developing below detection threshold (unaware case: crew continue duties and take no action)
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Unaware case: the function definition does not state how much authority is lost before it becomes detectable, nor whether it manifests as a manoeuvre limit reached or as departure. Missing: the detection threshold, the crew-awareness mechanism, and whether the reversion path recovers the case — cannot derive an aircraft effect or class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous yaw response to crew command (yaw surface responds incorrectly relative to commanded input)
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The function definition does not state the magnitude or sign of the erroneous yaw response; the aircraft effect ranges from a controllable transient to a directional upset. Missing: the amount and type of error to derive an aircraft effect and class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded yaw motion with no crew command (rudder/yaw surface deflection without input)
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The function definition does not state the magnitude or rate of the uncommanded yaw; effect ranges from a nuisance sideslip to a directional departure, and interacts with the sized engine-out directional case. Missing: the deflection magnitude/rate to derive an aircraft effect and class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of yaw control authority
fha.effAc: Aircraft loses directional control authority; unable to counter asymmetric thrust (outboard engine-out at 28 m moment arm is the stated directional-control sizing case) or crosswind; loss of controlled flight not shown to be recoverable.
fha.effCrew: Crew unable to maintain heading/track; excessive workload with no effective means of directional control.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of directional control authority with no alternate means, against a design case (outboard engine-out at V1 with max blade payload) that yaw control must cover, is consistent with loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded yaw authority outside manoeuvre limits

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous pressurisation control of the fuselage differential (control commands a differential different from the scheduled value, crew aware via avionics differential/cabin-altitude indication)
fha.effAc: Fuselage differential driven away from schedule; positive/negative mechanical relief remains available to protect structure independently of the control system
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted by differential/cabin-altitude indication; select manual pressurisation mode / alternate controller; increased workload managing the excursion
fha.effPax: N/A — hold unoccupied in flight, flight crew only
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Direction and magnitude of the erroneous differential (toward positive over-pressure vs cabin-altitude climb) and the resulting crew cabin-altitude exposure are not bounded in the SDD; whether crew oxygen covers the exposure is not stated. Cannot derive a class without the exposure and oxygen-adequacy inputs.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Excessive negative fuselage differential driven toward the structural limit (external pressure exceeding internal beyond intended, control system commanding or failing to arrest the condition)
fha.effAc: Negative differential grows toward structural limit; independent negative pressure relief valve protects the structure independently of the control system
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted; select manual mode; the mechanical relief limits the structural excursion without crew action
fha.effPax: N/A — hold unoccupied in flight, flight crew only
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Classification turns on whether the independent negative relief valve arrests the excursion below the structural limit in all cases; the SDD states independent relief exists but does not quantify its capacity versus the worst-case negative-differential rate. Cannot derive class without that structural margin.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded loss of differential producing a cabin-altitude excursion (both outflow valves or control driving fully open, crew aware via cabin-altitude alerting)
fha.effAc: Fuselage differential lost; cabin altitude climbs toward ambient at the current flight level; structure not endangered (over-pressure not the failure direction)
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted by cabin-altitude warning; don crew oxygen masks; initiate emergency descent to a safe altitude; high workload
fha.effPax: N/A — hold unoccupied in flight, flight crew only
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Depends on maximum cabin altitude reached at FL260 and whether the crew-oxygen system covers the time-of-useful-consciousness and diversion; the SDD states crew oxygen is sized for four occupants for the diversion time but the resulting cabin-altitude exposure and its severity are not bounded here. Cannot derive class without confirming oxygen adequacy against the excursion profile.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded differential drift developing below the alerting threshold (crew unaware; crew continue duties normally and take no action)
fha.effAc: Fuselage differential drifts slowly; cabin altitude rises undetected below the alerting threshold; no automatic corrective action credited
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware and take no action; insidious cabin-altitude rise without alerting; risk of incapacitation before recognition
fha.effPax: N/A — hold unoccupied in flight, flight crew only
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Unaware slow-drift severity hinges on how far cabin altitude can rise before any independent means (relief, cross-check, physiological cue) triggers recognition, and on crew-oxygen coverage — none of which is bounded in the SDD. The absence of alerting is exactly what makes this potentially severe, but the effect chain is not closed by the provided inputs. Cannot derive class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded pressurisation control operating on a reduced schedule (single-controller or single-outflow-valve operation, crew aware)
fha.effAc: Pressurisation maintained on a reduced control schedule with remaining controller/outflow valve; differential held within limits at possibly reduced margin
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted to degraded configuration; monitor; possible flight-level restriction; slight increase in workload
fha.effPax: N/A — hold unoccupied in flight, flight crew only
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD states either controller and either outflow valve alone is sufficient, so the remaining capability appears adequate on a reduced schedule; however whether the degradation imposes a safety-margin or flight-level restriction (Minor vs No Safety Effect) is not quantified. Left blank pending the reduced-schedule performance and any operational limitation.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fuselage pressurisation control
fha.effAc: Fuselage cannot maintain the design differential; cabin/hold altitude follows ambient up to the maximum operating altitude (FL260). Structural relief valves remain independent per SDD, so overpressure is protected mechanically; the effect is loss of pressure retention control, not structural rupture.
fha.effCrew: Cabin-altitude alerting drives donning of crew oxygen masks and an emergency descent to a safe altitude; increased workload managing the descent and diversion. Crew oxygen provision is sized for four occupants for the diversion time at maximum operating altitude.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects support a large reduction in safety margin requiring an emergency descent, but the classification (Hazardous vs Major) turns on the physiological exposure at FL260 with functioning crew oxygen and the availability/timeliness of emergency descent — a judgement dependent on the maximum-altitude cabin-altitude excursion and oxygen duration that the function definition alone does not fix. Confirm severity against the AC 25.1309 depressurisation guidance.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced conditioning capacity on single-source (single-pack) operation
fha.effAc: One air cycle pack lost; the remaining pack operates on a reduced hold conditioning schedule per the SDD. Flight-deck conditioning is maintained; hold conditioning is degraded.
fha.effCrew: Slight increase in crew workload managing the degraded configuration and monitoring; flight-deck environment maintained.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied, so the reduced hold schedule has no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Single-pack operation is an accepted degraded configuration ('Single-pack operation is permitted with a reduced hold conditioning schedule'); the residual effect is a slight increase in crew workload with the flight deck maintained and no occupant impact. Confirm the flight deck remains within conditioning limits on one pack. [anchor MIN-2 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous air conditioning or distribution
fha.effAc: Air delivered at an incorrect temperature or to the wrong zone. If the flight deck receives excessively hot/cold or contaminated air, the crew's environment is degraded; pressure control is unaffected.
fha.effCrew: Potential thermal discomfort or, in the worst case (e.g. smoke/fume ingress via conditioning), physical distress and increased workload; crew becomes aware through cabin environment and system status.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — 'Erroneous air conditioning or distribution' spans benign mis-temperature through to a fume/contamination case; the function definition does not resolve which erroneous outcome bounds the condition, so the aircraft/crew effect that drives severity cannot be fixed. Split into distinct malfunction conditions (e.g. erroneous temperature vs contaminated-air distribution) or state the worst-case erroneous output before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of distribution to one conditioning zone
fha.effAc: Conditioned air ceases to one of the two separate zones (flight deck or hold). If the affected zone is the hold, no occupant effect (unoccupied); if the flight deck, its ventilation/temperature is lost.
fha.effCrew: Effect on crew depends entirely on which zone is lost: negligible if the hold; loss of flight-deck ventilation/temperature with rising discomfort if the flight deck.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The two conditioning zones (flight deck vs hold) have very different consequences and the condition as stated does not name which zone. Cannot classify a single worst case without deciding whether flight-deck loss is the bounding case (crew distress/workload) or the hold is (no occupant effect). Specify the zone, or split into flight-deck-loss and hold-loss conditions, then classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of probe heating or detection capability — some heated probes or one detection function degraded, coverage reduced
fha.effAc: Reduced probe-heat coverage or detection capability narrows protection margin in icing; individually monitored elements annunciate a lost element, and redundant probes/detection remain
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted to the lost element and manage remaining probe heat/detection; increased monitoring workload
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground an aircraft-level severity from the function definition alone: the outcome depends on WHICH probes/detection elements are lost and how much air-data / icing-awareness redundancy remains after that loss. Probes are monitored individually and lost elements are annunciated, but the residual-capability analysis (how many independent air-data sources survive, standby coverage) is not in the provided material. Confirm against the air-data architecture before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous or misleading flight and navigation information presented to the crew
fha.effAc: Crew act on incorrect attitude, air data or navigation state; with fly-by-wire primary control and operation in the low flight levels, agreed-erroneous presentation can drive an unrecovered flight-path excursion or controlled flight into terrain.
fha.effCrew: Crew have no independent basis to detect the error if the misleading data is presented as valid; excessive workload attempting to reconcile displays against the standby instrument.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected misleading flight/navigation information can lead to loss of the aeroplane; proposed for engineer confirmation. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of flight and navigation information presentation
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the function definition and provided material do not state WHICH information is lost or how much presentation capability remains, and PL severity turns entirely on the remaining capability and the affected phase. Provide the specific loss content and the flight phase to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of flight and navigation information presentation
fha.effAc: Primary display presentation lost; the SDD documents an independent standby instrument (attitude, airspeed, altitude on the DC essential bus) sharing no supply, sensor or processing with the primaries, providing a survivable but degraded means of flight. Large reduction in safety margins.
fha.effCrew: High crew workload flying on standby information only, particularly in the approach/landing phase to a semi-prepared strip.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Proposed Hazardous (not Catastrophic) because an independent standby instrument sharing nothing with the primaries provides a degraded means of continued flight — a large reduction in safety margins and high crew workload rather than loss of the aeroplane. Contingent on the standby genuinely being independent (SDD claim) and adequate for the approach/landing case; confirm. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous, missing or mis-prioritised crew alerting (crew acts on, or fails to act on, a false picture of aircraft state)
fha.effAc: Crew alerting is the single consolidated means by which failures are made known to the crew; erroneous or mis-prioritised alerting can lead the crew to take an inappropriate action or fail to take a required one against an actual system state, potentially defeating a mitigation the safety case depends on.
fha.effCrew: Crew responds to a false or mis-ordered picture: either acts on a non-existent condition or is diverted from the true condition; workload and error potential increase materially.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect severity depends on WHICH underlying condition is masked or misrepresented and on the crew's opportunity to detect the error by other means — a combination the aircraft-function definition and SDD do not resolve. Worst-case (erroneous alerting causing the crew to actively disable a functioning system, or masking a catastrophic condition) trends toward Catastrophic, but that requires a specified concurrent failure. Left empty pending the paired underlying failure condition and any independent crew cross-check.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to annunciate an actual system failure (a real failure occurs and no alert is presented)
fha.effAc: An actual system failure progresses unannunciated; the crew continues normal duties and takes no corrective or reconfiguration action, so any manual mitigation the safety case relies on is not initiated and the underlying failure develops uncontained.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of the failure; no action taken; first indication may be a secondary consequence, compressing the time available to respond.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity is set by the severity of the un-annunciated underlying failure and by whether it required crew action to remain survivable — a value that cannot be derived from the alerting function alone. Cannot classify without the specific masked failure condition; left empty per abstention rather than assigning a benign class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Incorrectly prioritised alert presentation (correct alerts shown but in the wrong order/priority)
fha.effAc: Alerts are present but their ordering does not reflect urgency; the crew may address a lower-priority condition first and delay the response to a higher-priority one, degrading the timeliness of a required mitigation.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload to reconcile the alert list; risk of delayed response to the governing condition; task-shedding under time pressure.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect ranges from a workload increase (Minor/Major) to a delayed response that lets a serious condition progress (higher), depending on which conditions are co-present and the phase. The alerting function definition does not fix which conditions coincide, so the driving effect cannot be derived here; left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of crew alerting (alerting capability reduced but not lost across all systems)
fha.effAc: Alerting is degraded on one of two independent processing channels or for a reduced set of conditions; primary alerting remains for most systems, but coverage or redundancy of the annunciation of subsequent failures is reduced.
fha.effCrew: Crew retains alerting for most conditions; degraded-alerting state is itself annunciated; increased vigilance and workload to compensate for reduced coverage.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — With one of two independent channels remaining, immediate effect is a reduction in alerting redundancy rather than loss of the crew's picture; this trends toward Major (significant reduction in a safety-related functional capability), but the row depends on the degraded state being annunciated and on retained coverage — not fully established by the SDD. Left empty pending confirmation of retained coverage and self-annunciation.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of alerting for a subset of systems (alerting fully lost for some systems, retained for others)
fha.effAc: Failures within the affected subset progress unannunciated while alerting for other systems continues; the crew has no indication of, and takes no action on, failures in the un-alerted subset.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of failures in the affected subset; normal duties continued for those systems; alerting retained elsewhere may create a false sense of full coverage.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Equivalent to SF-019-M2 scoped to a subset: severity is governed by the most severe un-alerted condition within that subset and its need for crew action, which the alerting function alone does not fix. Cannot classify without the identity of the affected subset; left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of crew alerting
fha.effAc: No consolidated, prioritised annunciation of any system failure or hazard state; subsequent failures are presented to the crew, if at all, only through individual system indications without prioritisation or associated procedures.
fha.effCrew: Crew loses the single prioritised means of learning what has failed and what to do about it; latent or developing failures may go unrecognised, delaying or preventing correct response; greatly increased workload and error potential in a compound-failure sequence.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of the aircraft's sole consolidated alerting means removes the crew's primary means of detecting and correctly responding to further failures; in a compound-failure sequence this can prevent timely recognition of a condition leading to loss of the airplane. Classified on worst-case across phases. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to detect an actual fire or overheat condition
fha.effAc: An actual fire or overheat in a monitored zone (engine nacelle, APU compartment, bleed-duct run, main gear bay, or hold) is not annunciated; no extinguishing is commanded and the fire may propagate. The hold has smoke detection but no suppression, so an undetected fire has no independent means of arrest.
fha.effCrew: Crew continues normally and takes no action; the first indication may be secondary damage or structural/systems failure, by which point response may be ineffective.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An undetected fire/overheat in a fire zone can propagate uncontrolled, and with no hold suppression fitted an undetected hold fire has no independent means of arrest; the credible outcome is loss of the airplane. Worst-case across zones and phases. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of fire and overheat detection coverage
fha.effAc: Detection coverage is lost over part of the monitored set of zones; whether a fire zone is left with no detection, and which one, is not determinable from the aircraft-function statement.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify at aircraft level from the function definition alone: the aircraft-level consequence depends on WHICH zone loses coverage (a monitored fire zone left undetected approaches the SF-020-M2 outcome; a redundant/overheat-only run is far less severe). The zone-by-zone detection allocation is an SFHA/architecture input, not an aircraft-function effect — required before a severity can be derived. Severity left empty per abstention rule.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded single-loop detection following loss of one loop
fha.effAc: With one detection loop lost the affected zone reverts from AND-logic dual-loop warning to single-loop logic; detection remains available but the design margin against spurious and against missed detection is reduced for that zone.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Detection is retained after loss of one loop (degrades to single-loop logic), so this is not a loss of the detection function; the aircraft-level effect is a reduction in detection integrity margin whose severity depends on which zone and on the residual single-loop reliability — neither derivable from the aircraft-function statement. Likely a slight reduction in safety margin, but the aircraft effect is not grounded enough to commit a class. Severity left empty per abstention rule.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire and overheat detection
fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: No detection of fire or overheat in engine nacelles, APU compartment, bleed duct runs or main gear bays; a developing fire progresses without annunciation and without cueing extinguisher discharge, permitting structural damage in a fire zone before any crew response is possible.
fha.effCrew: Crew receive no fire/overheat warning; they cannot initiate the fire handles or diagnose the event through this function; loss of the primary cue to shut down and isolate an affected engine/APU.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect beyond the airframe consequence.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected fire/overheat in a fire zone (nacelle/APU/bleed/gear bay) is a large reduction in safety margins — the crew loses the sole cue to extinguish and isolate; consistent with dual-loop detection being provided precisely because undetected fire is severe. Proposed for engineer confirmation; whether it reaches Catastrophic depends on effects of an undetected uncontrolled nacelle fire, which the SDD does not resolve. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent agent discharge into an intact nacelle
fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: One extinguisher bottle of an engine pair is expended into a nacelle with no fire; that bottle is no longer available for a genuine fire in either nacelle of the pair (bottles are cross-plumbed to serve the pair), leaving only the second bottle for a subsequent real event on that side.
fha.effCrew: Spurious discharge indication; crew must diagnose a false fire cue and manage a reduced-agent state; the affected engine may be shut down unnecessarily.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of one of two bottles per engine pair is a significant reduction in the fire-suppression safety margin plus increased crew workload from the false cue, but redundancy (second bottle, cross-plumbed) remains for a real fire. Proposed for confirmation. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Agent discharged to the wrong nacelle
fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: On a real fire, agent is delivered to the intact nacelle of the pair rather than the burning one; the fire in the affected nacelle continues uncontrolled while a bottle is consumed on the wrong side, leaving only the remaining bottle to reach the actual fire.
fha.effCrew: Crew observe a persistent fire warning after a discharge that should have suppressed it; must recognise the mis-routing and discharge the second bottle to the correct nacelle under time pressure.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Condition is not represented in the current FCIM (model carries SF-021-M as the mis-routing case); the SDD states bottles are cross-plumbed to either nacelle of a pair but does not describe a mechanism by which agent is delivered to the wrong nacelle, nor the aircraft-level effect of an uncontrolled nacelle fire. Cannot ground an aircraft effect firmly enough to derive severity — confirm whether this condition is intended and provide the mis-selection effect before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent automatic APU discharge with aircraft unattended
fha.effAc: The single dedicated APU bottle discharges automatically with no APU fire present; the APU fire-suppression provision is expended and unavailable for a subsequent genuine APU fire until recharged.
fha.effCrew: Aircraft unattended by definition of this condition; no crew present to observe or respond at the time of discharge; discovered subsequently as an expended-bottle/dispatch item.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants present.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is a ground, unattended, aircraft-not-operating state with loss of the single APU suppression provision until recharge; the SDD confirms automatic unattended APU discharge exists but does not state the aircraft-level safety consequence of an unavailable APU bottle, and there is no in-flight/occupant exposure to drive a class. Insufficient stated effect to derive severity — confirm the dispatch/continued-airworthiness consequence before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Agent delivered to only one nacelle of a pair
fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: On a genuine fire, suppression reaches only one nacelle of the pair; if the fire is in that nacelle it is addressed, but the cross-plumbed capability to direct the remaining bottle to either nacelle is degraded, reducing the ability to fight a fire on the paired nacelle or to apply a second shot to the same nacelle.
fha.effCrew: Reduced suppression flexibility; crew may find the second bottle cannot be directed as intended and must manage the fire with degraded agent-delivery options.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Partial loss of the cross-plumbed two-bottles-per-pair capability is a significant reduction in the fire-suppression margin, but suppression to the affected nacelle can still be achieved; not a total loss. Proposed for confirmation; escalates toward Hazardous if the residual capability cannot reach the actual fire, which the SDD does not resolve. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of automatic APU extinguishing while unattended (partial loss of fire-extinguishing function) — an APU compartment fire is detected but the automatic discharge does not occur with the aircraft unattended on the ground
fha.effAc: APU compartment fire is not suppressed on the ground with the aircraft unattended; fire may propagate from the aft fuselage APU fire zone before crew or ground personnel intervene. Detection remains available (dual-loop) but the automatic suppression relied on for the unattended state is lost.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried. On the ground the aircraft is unattended by definition of this condition.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a §25.1309 class from the SDD alone. The document establishes automatic APU discharge on the ground with the aircraft unattended and that the APU compartment is a fire zone, but gives no ground-fire propagation outcome, no exposure/attendance assumptions, and no aircraft-level effect on continued airworthiness. Ground-only, unattended failure conditions turn on operational and structural-propagation assumptions not stated here; classify only after the ground-fire scenario and attendance concept are defined.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: No fire-extinguishing agent delivered when commanded (total loss of extinguishing) — an engine or APU fire is detected and the crew commands discharge but no agent reaches the affected zone
fha.effAc: An engine nacelle fire cannot be extinguished by the fixed system after the crew fire-handle command; fire continues in a high-energy, flammable-fluid fire zone adjacent to the wing and its fuel, hydraulic and electrical services. Fuel shut-off and fire-handle isolation remain available, but the means to extinguish is lost. Uncontrolled nacelle fire can threaten the wing structure and the fuel tanks.
fha.effCrew: Crew execute the fire drill (fire handle, fuel shut-off) but have no fixed extinguishing available; workload and decision demand increase and a diversion is forced.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects support a severe outcome (uncontained nacelle fire near wing/fuel), but the SDD does not state the aircraft-level consequence of a sustained, non-extinguished engine fire (e.g. time to structural/fuel involvement, whether continued safe flight and landing is retained). Do not commit a class until the fire-propagation timeline and the credit taken for shut-off/isolation are established; abstaining rather than reaching for Catastrophic without that basis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced oxygen supply duration or reserve (partial loss) — crew breathing oxygen remains available on demand but the stored quantity/duration is below the sized value
fha.effAc: No aircraft handling effect. Available crew oxygen endurance for a depressurisation/smoke diversion is reduced below the sized four-occupant duration-plus-reserve.
fha.effCrew: Crew retain breathing oxygen on demand but with reduced duration for the descent and diversion that follow a loss of pressurisation, smoke or fume event; margin for a prolonged diversion is eroded.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity depends on HOW reduced the duration is relative to the diversion time at maximum operating altitude, which the SDD sizes to but does not quantify for a degraded case. A slight reduction points to Minor; a reduction that cannot cover the required diversion points higher. Cannot ground the class without the sized duration and the residual-endurance threshold; leaving empty rather than guessing mid-scale.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of supply to one mask station (partial loss) — oxygen is not delivered at one of the four mask stations while the other stations remain supplied
fha.effAc: No aircraft handling effect. Nominal crew complement is two with provision for four; a single mask station is unavailable while the remaining stations and the common manifold supply are intact.
fha.effCrew: The affected crew position loses its oxygen supply for a depressurisation/smoke/fume event; regulators are independent per mask, so other stations are unaffected. With a nominal two-crew complement, a spare/alternate station is available, but a crew member at the failed station is unprotected until relocated.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity depends on the operational assumption of which/how many crew are on station and whether relocation to an unaffected mask is credited — the SDD gives four mask stations, independent regulators, and a nominal two/provision-for-four complement, but not the crew-station concept that drives the effect on a required crew member during a depressurisation. Cannot classify without that operational input; abstaining.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of stored oxygen quantity
fha.effCrew: If undetected in flight, reduced oxygen reserve would only manifest when the masks are demanded on a subsequent pressurisation/smoke event, shortening protected duration; SDD states cylinder pressure is displayed continuously and is a dispatch item, so an aircraft-level effect for the undetected case cannot be stated without the failure mode that defeats indication.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric reverse thrust on the ground (reverse deployed/commanded unequally between the two inboard engines during landing rollout)
fha.effAc: Yawing moment from asymmetric reverse on a semi-prepared strip; directional deviation during rollout with reduced tracking margin against the 1,800 m landing requirement (~1,080 m predicted rollout). Reverse is inboard-engine only, so asymmetry arm is smaller than an outboard case.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the yaw and correct with nose-wheel steering and differential braking; increased workload during rollout.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a severity: the directional-control margin on a semi-prepared surface at the inboard reverse moment arm, and whether crew steering/braking correction is sufficient, is not stated in the provided definitions — needs a controllability/performance assessment before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric reverse thrust developing below detection threshold during landing rollout (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: Gradual asymmetric deceleration builds an uncorrected yaw/track deviation on a semi-prepared strip; with the crew taking no corrective action the deviation consumes rollout margin against the 1,800 m requirement and risks lateral departure from the strip.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue rollout duties normally and take no action regarding the undetected asymmetry until the deviation becomes apparent, by which point correction margin is reduced.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a severity: the outcome depends on how large the sub-threshold asymmetry can grow, the lateral margin of the semi-prepared strip, and the point of eventual crew detection — none quantified in the provided material. Requires controllability/performance analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced ground reverse thrust (partial loss — reverse available but at reduced level, e.g. one inboard reverser inoperative)
fha.effAc: Less reverse deceleration on the semi-prepared strip; increased reliance on wheel braking to stop within the 1,800 m requirement against ~1,080 m predicted rollout. Margin between requirement and predicted rollout is the basis on which braking/deceleration degradation is assessed.
fha.effCrew: Crew apply braking; awareness of degraded stopping performance; increased workload on a short semi-prepared surface.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a severity: whether reverse thrust is credited in the landing distance, and how much rollout margin partial reverse loss consumes, is not stated — the ~720 m margin is described as the basis for assessing braking degradation, not quantified per contributor. Needs performance credit analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground reverse thrust (no reverse deceleration available on landing)
fha.effAc: No reverse-thrust deceleration; the aircraft relies wholly on wheel braking (carbon multi-disc, dual hydraulic supply plus accumulator) to stop within the 1,800 m requirement against ~1,080 m predicted rollout on a semi-prepared surface. Effect depends on whether reverse is credited in the certified landing distance.
fha.effCrew: Crew use maximum wheel braking; awareness of loss of a deceleration means; increased workload on a short strip.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a severity: if reverse is NOT credited in the landing distance the effect may be minor, but if it IS credited on the semi-prepared surface the loss erodes stopping margin — the credit basis is not stated in the provided material. Needs landing-performance/credit determination before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous roll response to crew command (roll surfaces respond in the wrong sense or magnitude relative to the commanded roll)
fha.effAc: Aircraft rolls other than as commanded; loss of predictable roll control of the trajectory. Erroneous/reversed roll response during a critical phase (takeoff, approach, low altitude, or the engine-out blade-loaded case) can produce an unrecoverable attitude excursion.
fha.effCrew: Crew face a control response inconsistent with input; recovery may be impossible in the time and altitude available depending on phase and magnitude.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous roll response is a malfunction of a primary control-of-trajectory function; an incorrect/reversed roll response at low altitude or in a critical phase can cause loss of the aircraft, consistent with the existing Catastrophic classification of roll total-loss (SF-003-TL) and the malfunction pattern used for pitch/yaw erroneous-response conditions in this model. Engineer to confirm against a controllability assessment. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded roll motion with no crew command
fha.effAc: Uncommanded roll displaces the aircraft from the commanded flight path; if the crew cannot arrest and reverse it the bank develops to an unrecoverable attitude and loss of control.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the uncommanded motion and apply immediate corrective roll input; high workload with reduced margin, especially at low altitude on approach/landing.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded roll that can progress to an unrecoverable attitude and loss of the airplane; effects support the highest class. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded roll divergence below detection threshold (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: A slow roll divergence below the detection threshold accumulates unopposed; with no crew correction the bank builds to a large attitude excursion and progresses toward loss of control.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties and take no corrective action until the divergence becomes apparent, by which point recovery margin may be lost; late recognition drives very high workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Unaware case: the crew take no action, the divergence progresses to an unrecoverable attitude; loss of the airplane supports the highest class. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded roll authority within manoeuvre limits
fha.effAc: Roll control remains available but at reduced authority/rate; the aircraft is controllable and manoeuvres remain achievable within the manoeuvre limits, with reduced margin against demanding cases.
fha.effCrew: Crew adapt to reduced roll response; annunciated degraded state raises workload but the task remains manageable within limits.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Roll retained within manoeuvre limits: a significant reduction in functional capability / safety margin and increased crew workload, not a large reduction; effects support Major. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded roll authority outside manoeuvre limits (roll control retained but insufficient for full manoeuvre envelope)
fha.effAc: Roll control is retained but authority falls short of the manoeuvre limits, leaving the aircraft unable to meet demanding roll cases (e.g. crosswind, upset, engine-out asymmetry); a large reduction in safety margin.
fha.effCrew: Crew must fly within a restricted roll envelope with excessive workload to stay inside the reduced capability, particularly at low altitude and in the engine-out sizing case.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Control retained but authority insufficient for the full manoeuvre envelope: a large reduction in functional capability and excessive crew workload; effects support Hazardous. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded roll authority developing below detection threshold (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: Roll authority erodes below the detection threshold while the crew remain unaware; the shortfall is not manifest until a roll demand exceeds the remaining authority.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties and take no action; the degradation only becomes apparent when a manoeuvre demand is not met.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD does not state roll-authority monitoring/detection coverage or crew-alerting behaviour, so whether the unaware erosion reaches a margin-critical shortfall before manifesting is undetermined. Need the roll-authority detection threshold and the worst-case roll demand assumed while unaware.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded yaw authority within manoeuvre limits
fha.effAc: Yaw control retained but at reduced authority; sizing case is an outboard engine failure at V1 with maximum blade payload, and rudder is split so a single supply loss must still leave sufficient authority. Within-limits degradation leaves controllable directional response.
fha.effCrew: Increased attention to directional control; no exceptional skill required within manoeuvre limits.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Within-manoeuvre-limits yaw degradation is a slight reduction in safety margins per the split-rudder sizing that retains sufficient authority on a single supply loss. [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded high-lift movement with no crew command
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Cannot derive a severity without the stated aircraft effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous high-lift response to crew selection
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — No aircraft-level effect of an erroneous high-lift position is stated in the SDD; high-lift position feeds the performance computation but the consequence of a wrong position on speed/margin is not given. fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric high-lift deployment between sides
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8).
