Cannot derive severity without the stated aircraft effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of high-lift configuration capability
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD ties high-lift to configuration and the performance computation but states no aircraft-level effect of being unable to configure — e.g. approach-speed increase or landing-distance impact against the 1,800 m semi-prepared requirement. Cannot classify without that effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous gear position or downlock indication
fha.effAc: Indicated gear/downlock state does not match true state; a not-down-and-locked gear may be indicated locked, or a locked gear indicated unsafe. On the mismatch that hides a not-locked unit, gear may collapse on touchdown/rollout with loss of ground support at one or more units.
fha.effCrew: Crew relies on a false safe indication and completes the landing, or reacts to a false unsafe indication (go-around, alternate extension) unnecessarily; erroneous indication defeats the take-off/landing configuration check.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A false 'down-and-locked' that conceals an unlocked unit can lead to gear collapse on a semi-prepared strip with a large reduction in ground-handling/safety margins; proposed Hazardous. Confirm whether independent dual downlock sensing per unit downgrades the undetected case. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of downlock confirmation on one unit
fha.effAc: One of the two independent downlock sensing circuits on one unit is lost; downlock confirmation for that unit is degraded but the unit may still be down and locked, and the second sensing circuit remains.
fha.effCrew: Crew sees an unsafe or unconfirmed indication for one unit; assumed to apply the abnormal procedure (alternate/free-fall extension, visual/manual confirmation) before committing to land.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of one of two independent downlock confirmations on a single unit, with the second sensing circuit retained and free-fall alternate available, is a significant increase in crew workload and reduction of margin, not a loss of ground support; proposed Major. Confirm. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground support / flotation capability
fha.effAc: Aircraft cannot be supported on its gear on the ground; touchdown/rollout with no ground support results in fuselage/structure ground contact and loss of the airframe.
fha.effCrew: No means available to arrest or control the aircraft on the surface; outcome not recoverable by crew action.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of ground support at landing results in loss of the airplane; proposed Catastrophic. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous braking response to pedal command
fha.effAc: Braking does not match the pedal command — either symmetric over/under-braking eroding the stopping margin, or asymmetric braking generating an uncommanded yaw during a high-energy stop on a semi-prepared strip of limited width, risking directional excursion.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect and counter the erroneous braking with steering/differential input during a high-workload deceleration; corrective margin is small given the 1,800 m requirement against a ~1,080 m predicted rollout.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Asymmetric erroneous braking during a high-energy stop on a limited-width semi-prepared strip is a large reduction in directional-control margin with high crew workload; proposed Hazardous, but confirm against the directional-control/runway-width study — a purely symmetric error retaining stopping capability within margin may be Major. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of wheel braking capability
fha.effAc: No wheel braking available (normal, alternate and accumulator reserve exhausted or lost). On the 1,800 m semi-prepared requirement against a ~1,080 m predicted rollout, loss of all braking removes the stopping margin and leads to an overrun beyond the prepared surface.
fha.effCrew: Crew has no wheel braking; residual deceleration (inboard reversers, aerodynamic) is insufficient to stop within the strip; outcome not recoverable within the available distance.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of wheel braking on a 1,800 m semi-prepared strip drives an overrun with likely loss of the airplane; proposed Catastrophic. Confirm whether reverser plus accumulator-reserve architecture and overrun terrain modify the worst-case outcome — accumulator is sized for six applications with all three hydraulic systems lost, so a true total loss is a further-degraded state. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to annunciate an actual loss of restraint tension (real tension loss occurs but is not alerted; crew continues normally and takes no action)
fha.effAc: A genuine loss of strap tension at one or more stations is not annunciated; with two straps per saddle and neighbour load-sharing (SDD §5.8.3) a single-strap loss is carried, but a developing multi-strap or multi-station loss progresses undetected toward a longitudinal restraint shortfall on a single 72.6 t unitised blade.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware; no indication and no in-flight restraint adjustment available (SDD §5.8.6), so no corrective or precautionary action is taken.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Monitoring-failure severity derives from the worst undetected restraint condition it masks. The SDD gives the restraint redundancy (two straps/saddle, neighbour sharing) and the annunciation logic (single-strap annunciated; two-adjacent-stations = immediate-attention condition, §5.8.2) but does NOT quantify how much restraint capacity can be lost, or how far the blade can shift, before CG/structural limits are exceeded. Without that aircraft-level effect the class of losing the annunciation cannot be derived; left empty pending restraint-loss-versus-controllability data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to annunciate an actual loss of restraint tension (monitoring loop fails to alert a real tension loss; crew-unaware case)
fha.effAc: An actual restraint-tension loss develops without annunciation; the single instrumented tension loop (SDD §5.8.3) failing to alert removes the sole in-flight means by which a developing longitudinal restraint shortfall on the single unitised blade would be recognised.
fha.effCrew: Crew continues duties normally with no alert; no action taken, and no in-flight restraint adjustment is possible even if aware (SDD §5.8.6).
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Same abstention basis as SF-013-M2: the SDD establishes the loop is a single instrumented run and the annunciation thresholds, but does not state the magnitude of undetected restraint loss or blade displacement that would threaten CG/structural integrity. The aircraft-level effect of losing the annunciation cannot be derived without that data; severity left empty rather than guessed.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of restraint-tension monitoring over part of the payload length (monitoring degraded; a portion of the hold is no longer instrumented, remaining coverage intact)
fha.effAc: Tension monitoring is lost over part of the hold length; restraint hardware is unaffected, but any tension loss arising within the unmonitored segment would develop without annunciation. Restraint neighbour load-sharing (SDD §5.8.3) still carries a single-strap loss.
fha.effCrew: Crew retains monitoring over the remainder of the hold; degraded coverage is annunciated, and crew may apply added conservatism, but no in-flight restraint adjustment is available (SDD §5.8.6).
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — A partial monitoring loss leaves an unmonitored segment where a restraint loss could develop undetected. Whether losing coverage over part of the length is Minor (slight reduction in margins, remaining coverage adequate) or higher depends on how much undetected restraint loss the unmonitored segment could permit and its blade-shift/CG consequence — not quantified in the SDD. Class not derivable; left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of restraint-tension monitoring coverage at one or more stations (monitoring lost at discrete stations, monitoring retained elsewhere)
fha.effAc: Monitoring is lost at one or more discrete saddle stations; a tension loss at an unmonitored station would not be annunciated. Restraint capacity is unaffected and neighbour load-sharing still applies for a single-strap loss (SDD §5.8.3).
fha.effCrew: Crew retains monitoring at the remaining stations; the loss of station coverage is indicated, but no in-flight restraint adjustment is possible (SDD §5.8.6).
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Loss of monitoring at discrete stations with coverage retained elsewhere. Whether an undetected tension loss at an unmonitored station is benign (neighbour-carried, single strap) or leads to a significant restraint shortfall depends on how many stations lose coverage and the restraint margin at each — the SDD gives the two-strap/neighbour architecture but not the aircraft-level restraint-loss threshold. Class not derivable; left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of restraint-tension monitoring (no strap tension is monitored or annunciated over the full hold)
fha.effAc: The single instrumented tension loop is lost entirely (SDD §5.8.3); no strap tension is monitored anywhere in the hold and no tension-loss annunciation is available. Any developing restraint loss on the single 72.6 t unitised blade progresses wholly undetected, with no in-flight means of recognition. Restraint hardware itself is unaffected and neighbour load-sharing still carries a single-strap loss.
fha.effCrew: Crew has no restraint-tension indication for the entire flight and no in-flight restraint adjustment (SDD §5.8.6); the crew is unaware of any developing restraint condition and takes no action.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Complete loss of the sole in-flight restraint-tension detection on a single unitised 72.6 t payload could plausibly be significant, since it removes all warning of a developing restraint loss — but the aircraft-level consequence (blade shift, CG excursion, structural threat) that a totally undetected restraint loss could reach is not quantified in the SDD, and the base restraint architecture may itself preclude a hazardous outcome for a single-strap failure. The class of losing all monitoring therefore cannot be derived from the stated effects alone; left empty rather than reaching for a value. Note: the model classifies the restraint-provision TL (SF-012-TL) as Catastrophic; the monitoring TL should be assessed against the residual restraint reliability with monitoring absent.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of air conditioning and distribution
fha.effAc: No conditioned air delivered to flight deck or hold; pressurisation control (separate function SF-014) unaffected but conditioning/temperature/ventilation lost. Aircraft airworthy; crew environment degrades.
fha.effCrew: Loss of flight-deck ventilation and temperature control increases crew discomfort and workload over a diversion; crew don available means as required and divert.
fha.effPax: Hold is unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD establishes ECS conditions the flight deck and hold and that the hold is unoccupied, but does not state the flight-deck environmental limits, diversion time, or whether loss of conditioning alone (pressurisation retained via SF-014) produces distress or excessive workload sufficient for Major vs Hazardous. Cannot ground an aircraft-level severity — needs cabin-environment / diversion-duration data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous or asymmetric ice-protection activation
fha.effAc: Ice protection applied incorrectly or unequally across surfaces/inlets; asymmetric heating could leave a surface unprotected in icing while another is protected, or apply protection where unneeded.
fha.effCrew: Zone health is annunciated; crew reconfigure to available protection. Workload increase to manage asymmetry in icing conditions.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD states IPS protects surfaces/inlets/probes 'where accretion would be unacceptable' and that lost zones are annunciated, but does not state the aircraft-level consequence of an unprotected surface in the icing envelope (handling/performance loss) nor the magnitude of asymmetric effect. Cannot derive severity without the icing-envelope handling and accretion-consequence data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Ice protection failing on when not required, imposing performance penalty
fha.effAc: Ice protection (wing anti-ice) active when not required; bleed demand reduces pack capacity and a performance penalty applies. Aircraft remains controllable; performance margin reduced.
fha.effCrew: Performance penalty of wing anti-ice in use is applied automatically to the displayed performance; crew may select the system off. Slight workload to detect and deselect.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD states the performance penalty of wing anti-ice in use is applied automatically and the crew may deselect, but does not quantify the penalty (climb/cruise margin) or its consequence at the 1,800 m / ~1,080 m operating margins. Cannot ground whether the effect is a slight or significant reduction in safety margin — needs the anti-ice performance-penalty magnitude.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ice-protection coverage
fha.effAc: Some heated zones lost while others remain; a lost electrical zone is annunciated. Reduced protection over part of the protected surfaces/probes in the icing envelope.
fha.effCrew: Lost zone annunciated; crew manage exposure to icing (avoidance / exit) per available coverage. Workload increase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD states electrical zones are independently supplied and a lost zone is annunciated, but does not state which surfaces are safety-critical for accretion or the handling/performance consequence of an unprotected zone in the icing envelope. Cannot derive an aircraft-level severity without the accretion-consequence data per surface.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced protection capacity when heating demand shared
fha.effAc: IPS bleed demand shares the cross-bleed manifold with the ECS packs and reduces pack capacity when in use; under shared demand the available protection or conditioning capacity is reduced.
fha.effCrew: Crew manage bleed/pack configuration; workload increase to balance protection against conditioning demand.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD records that IPS makes 'a bleed demand to the environmental system that reduces pack capacity when in use' and that bleed is available from either side, but does not state the residual protection margin or whether shared demand leaves protection below the required level in the icing envelope. Cannot derive severity without the shared-demand capacity margins.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of airframe and inlet ice protection
fha.effAc: No protection on wing leading edges or engine inlet cowls; in the certification icing envelope, ice accretion on lifting surfaces and inlets degrades lift/drag and can disturb inlet flow to the four engines. Outside icing conditions there is no immediate effect.
fha.effCrew: Crew must avoid or exit icing; increased workload managing an unprotected airframe in or near icing conditions.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is conditional on encountering the icing envelope and on the accretion rate/degradation the airframe tolerates before control or thrust is affected — the SDD states the system exists 'for flight in the icing envelope of the certification basis' but gives no icing exposure or the aerodynamic/engine consequence needed to bound whether this is Hazardous or Catastrophic. Severity left blank pending the icing-envelope effects assessment.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous icing detection or masked detection
fha.effAc: Detection is advisory with automatic activation available; erroneous detection may command ice protection when not needed (unnecessary bleed/electrical demand, performance penalty applied) or mask a real icing condition so protection is not commanded automatically, allowing undetected accretion on surfaces, inlets and probes.
fha.effCrew: Crew may act on a false icing advisory or be denied a true one; the system 'may also be selected on manually', so crew can compensate if otherwise aware of icing.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Masked detection can allow undetected accretion including on probes/static ports feeding air data, but the aircraft effect depends on whether the crew is independently aware of icing (manual selection available) and on the accretion consequence — the SDD gives neither the icing exposure nor the air-data integrity consequence needed to select a class. Severity left blank.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to detect icing conditions that are present
fha.effAc: With automatic activation relied upon, a failure to detect real icing means ice protection is not automatically commanded, allowing accretion on wing/cowl, stabiliser zones and heated probes; probe accretion can corrupt air-data (airspeed, angle-of-attack) sensing. Manual selection remains available if the crew becomes aware by other means.
fha.effCrew: Crew receive no icing advisory; if unaware, they take no action and continue normally, allowing accretion to develop; if aware by other cues they can select protection on manually.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Undetected icing can degrade both aerodynamic performance and air-data integrity, but the class turns on the icing exposure and on whether loss of protection/air-data in icing is Hazardous or Catastrophic for this airframe — the SDD provides the architecture but not the icing-envelope effects or air-data consequence needed to derive severity. Severity left blank.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of one icing-detection channel
fha.effAc: Two ice detectors are installed on opposite sides of the forward fuselage; loss of one leaves the second detector providing icing detection with reduced redundancy. Detection capability is retained.
fha.effCrew: Reduced detection redundancy; manual selection of ice protection remains available; slight increase in monitoring.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Two detectors on opposite sides; loss of one leaves the second providing detection with the manual-selection path retained — a slight reduction in safety margin/redundancy with the function still available. The two detectors are 'identical in type', a common-cause item for CMA but not driving this single-channel-loss class. [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of probe heating and icing detection
fha.effAc: Loss of all probe/static/windshield heating and both ice detectors: in icing, unheated probes and static ports can ice over, corrupting airspeed and angle-of-attack sensing, and no icing advisory or automatic activation is available. Air-data corruption to the three ADIRUs affects primary flight information common across the aircraft.
fha.effCrew: No icing detection or advisory; unheated probes may produce misleading airspeed/AoA; crew workload rises and primary air-data integrity is threatened in icing.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This condition threatens air-data integrity feeding the primary displays as well as removing icing detection, which can be Hazardous or Catastrophic depending on remaining air-data means and icing exposure — the SDD notes the standby instrument shares nothing with the primaries, but does not state the air-data source topology under total probe-heat loss or the icing exposure, so the class cannot be derived. Severity left blank.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of primary flight and navigation display leaving standby information only
fha.effAc: Primary display presentation lost; independent integrated standby attitude, airspeed and altitude on the DC essential bus remains available, sharing no supply, sensor or processing with the primaries.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload flying on reduced standby information; diversion likely.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD establishes that a standby instrument remains after loss of the primary displays, so the effect is a reduction in capability and increase in workload rather than total loss — but the residual capability of standby-only flight in IFR at low flight levels (whether it is a significant or large reduction in safety margin) is not determinable from the function definition alone. Severity left empty pending the standby-only handling/workload assessment.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Cylinder overpressure vented overboard
fha.effAc: An overpressured oxygen cylinder is discharged overboard through the thermal discharge indicator; the second cylinder with crossover remains, either being capable of supplying the crew for the required duration at reduced reserve.
fha.effCrew: Reduced oxygen reserve; loss annunciated by low-pressure alerting and the skin discharge indicator; dispatch/diversion consequences.
fha.effPax: No passenger oxygen fitted; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD shows a two-cylinder crossover architecture where either cylinder can supply the crew at reduced reserve, so a single overboard vent is a reduction in reserve rather than a loss of supply. Whether the residual reserve after one cylinder is lost still meets the required diversion duration — hence whether this is Minor or Major — cannot be determined from the function definition; severity left empty pending the oxygen sizing/reserve assessment.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous or misleading flight and navigation information presented to the crew
fha.effAc: Aircraft flown to an erroneous state — deviation from intended trajectory, terrain/obstacle clearance or airspeed margin — because the crew act on misleading data. Independent standby instrument shares no supply, sensor or processing with the primaries, but detection of the discrepancy is not assured.
fha.effCrew: Crew act on false information; cross-check against the standby instrument required to detect and recover; potential to command an unsafe state before the discrepancy is identified.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; effect is on the airframe and crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Misleading flight/nav information acted upon can drive loss of control or CFIT; worst-case across phases is loss of the aircraft. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Masked fire and overheat detection — failure to annunciate an actual fire or overheat condition
fha.effAc: An actual nacelle, APU or bleed-duct fire/overheat is not annunciated; crew do not initiate extinguishing, allowing an undetected fire to progress in a fire zone containing flammable fluid and high energy.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of the fire; no fire-handle action taken; first indication is by secondary effects (thrust loss, smoke, structural damage) by which point response margin is degraded.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; effect is on the airframe and crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A masked (undetected) engine/APU fire defeats the sole means of crew-initiated extinguishing; unchecked fire in a nacelle can lead to loss of the aircraft. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: No breathing oxygen delivered to crew masks on demand
fha.effAc: With no oxygen at the masks during a loss-of-pressurisation, smoke or fume event, both pilots are exposed to hypoxia or the contaminant with no protective means; aircraft control is lost if the crew are incapacitated.
fha.effCrew: Crew unable to obtain breathing oxygen when donning masks; incapacitation during the descent/diversion the system is intended to protect; crew-only aircraft has no relief crew.
fha.effPax: No passenger oxygen fitted — hold is not occupied in flight; effect is on the crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of crew oxygen coincident with the event it protects against incapacitates both pilots; worst case is loss of the aircraft. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.
